source.title: Deep models reveal better strategies for superposition

record.file_problem: The text is the full post, but many mathematical expressions and some numerical values are missing or blank in the web extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses toy networks and reconstruction geometry rather than measuring natural-model neuron polysemanticity. Its own results test how superposition strategies change with decoder architecture and depth.
record.gate_note: The study reports results on toy networks with four independent features compressed to a 2D bottleneck. It does not test InceptionV1 neurons, language-model neurons, or the prevalence of polysemantic neurons in trained networks.
record.test_reason: The study takes superposition as given and asks which embedding geometries a toy 4-feature to 2D bottleneck network learns. Its intro says superposition yields polysemantic neurons, but it never measures neuron polysemanticity. It reports no share of mixed-response neurons, no neuron-level comparison with and without capacity pressure, and no polysemanticity count by architecture. The decoder-depth results concern feature geometry (symmetric, asymmetric, opened antipodal pairs) and reconstruction MSE, a related but different construct. These go under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that superposition geometry is shaped by model expressivity: uniform symmetric geometries are a fact about shallow decoders, not superposition itself. Deeper decoders exploit asymmetric and tilted embeddings, so embedding norm need not track importance. They also find that deeper models stop short of their best in-class decoder, with a gap of about 18%. Transfer to real networks is stated conditionally.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses an analogous feature-reconstruction task but a linear encoder followed by bilinear MLP decoders, rather than the tied-weight ReLU model used in Toy Models of Superposition. It also compares decoder depths and uses theoretical and binned-decoder benchmarks.
record.method_sensitivity: The geometry strategy changes with decoder depth/model class. Binned-decoder results also depend on bin resolution, though this is not a test of neuron-polysemanticity measurement.

fits_no_version.finding: With 4 equal features in a 2D bottleneck, tied ReLU and 1-bilinear-layer decoders give symmetric antipodal pairs (19/20 runs each). Decoders with 2–4 bilinear layers give asymmetric pairs, and with 3–4 layers mostly asymmetric plus opened pairs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The geometry of features in superposition depends on decoder expressivity/depth; uniform polytopes arise only with shallow decoders.

fits_no_version.finding: A single bilinear MLP reaches the best decoder of its class (0.0% gap). Four bilinear MLPs keep a gap that saturates near 18% with continued training and is not removed by retraining.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deeper toy decoders fail to converge to their best in-class solution for superposition reconstruction.

fits_no_version.finding: The binned-decoder MSE minimum for opening a pair lies at a finite angle that shrinks with finer bins.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The optimal superposition geometry depends on the decoder's resolution.

record.problems: The results are from a small toy setup with four features and a 2D bottleneck, not natural vision or language networks. The text reports 20 training runs per model type but no uncertainty estimates. The deeper model remains short of the best decoder in its class, and many expressions or values are missing from the web extraction.
record.rows_left_out: No additional numerical results extracted from the binned-decoder resolution figures; the relevant qualitative result is summarized under fits_no_version. Several other sweep values are missing from the supplied text.

untested.parts: No image classifiers or neurons studied.
Superposition is assumed. There is no neuron-level polysemanticity measurement and no comparison with a non-compressed setting.
No setting with enough dimensions for every feature.
Decoder depth is varied, but only embedding geometry and MSE are measured, not the share of polysemantic neurons.
Binned-decoder resolution is varied, but it scores reconstruction, not neuron polysemanticity classification.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked the geometry rows to V3 and V5 and labelled both as supported. That is wrong: the study never measures neuron polysemanticity, its prevalence, or its cause. It only mentions in the intro that superposition produces polysemantic neurons. All rows are relinked to 'none' and no verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: Image classifiers and their individual neurons.
Transformer language models, MLP neurons, and unrelated tokens or contexts.

The study examines a capacity-constrained toy setting, but does not compare it with a setting having enough dimensions for every feature or establish that capacity pressure is necessary for polysemanticity generally.
Polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure, including effects of initialization, regularization, or training noise.

The study varies decoder depth/model class in a toy network. It does not measure the share of polysemantic neurons, test SoLU or modern convnets, or show that lowering that share preserves performance.
Whether apparent mixed neuron activations in real models resolve into one shared feature or related jobs with better interpretability tools.
Whether counts of polysemantic neurons depend on activation range or explanation-scoring choices. The study varies binned-decoder resolution, not a neuron-polysemanticity measurement.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Toy networks with four features compressed into a 2D bottleneck
reader_labels.reason: The study demonstrates feature-packing geometries in this constrained setup and reports that the resulting geometry varies with decoder depth (r1-r5); it does not establish that capacity pressure is the only cause generally.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Tied ReLU and one-to-four bilinear-layer toy decoders
reader_labels.reason: The observed geometry classifications shift from mostly symmetric pairs in the tied-ReLU and one-layer cases to asymmetric and opened pairs in deeper cases (r1-r5).
